transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I just don’t care about the things I used to love doing anymore, even my projects in the garage and going out on the river. It's like all the joy has just been drained out of me, and I can't bring myself to do any of it.
How long have you been feeling this way, and have you ever experienced similar periods of low mood in the past?

I've been feeling this way for a little over two years now, starting not long after the big restructuring at my warehouse. I've never experienced a low period like this in the past; it all really began with that stress at work.
Have you ever had periods of time where you felt the opposite of depressed—unusually energetic, overly happy, needing much less sleep than usual, or feeling like your mind was racing?

No, I've never felt unusually energetic or happy like that; it's actually been the exact opposite, where I just feel heavy, slow, and completely drained. My mind does race sometimes when I'm lying in bed at night, but that's just from worrying and hearing that voice, not because I have any energy.
You mentioned hearing a voice when you're trying to sleep. Does it sound like a real person speaking to you from outside your head, and what does it say?

Yes, it sounds like a real man's voice speaking from right behind me, even when I know there's absolutely nobody there. He says awful things like, "You're dangerous, you're going to kill someone with that machine." It sounds completely real, like someone is standing right in the room with me.
To help me understand your history, have you ever had any other periods in your life—even years ago—where you felt depressed, down, or lost interest in things, even if it wasn't as severe as this?

No, I don't recall ever feeling this way before the problems at the warehouse started. I’ve always been a really steady, active guy who loved working on projects and staying busy. This is the first time in my life I've ever felt like this.
Did you start hearing this voice only after you began feeling depressed and drained, or have you ever heard it during times when your mood was completely fine?

Mostly, the voice and that heavy, depressed feeling started around the same time and have gone hand-in-hand. But there was a stretch last year where my wife thought my mood was a bit better and I wasn't feeling quite so crushed, yet I still heard that man's voice and was convinced my work badge was bugged. So even when the depression let up a little, those strange things in my head didn't go away.
During that period last year when you still heard the voice and believed your badge was bugged, would you say your mood had returned completely to normal, and how long did that last?

My mood didn't get completely back to normal, but I definitely felt a bit better—I wasn't crying as much or feeling quite as crushed. That stretch lasted for about a few weeks. But even though I felt a little lighter, I still heard that man's voice and was convinced my work badge was bugged.
Have you ever had a period of two weeks or more where you felt completely back to your normal, non-depressed self, but you were still hearing the voice or having those paranoid thoughts?

No, I never felt completely back to my normal self during that time, just a little bit lighter. But during those few weeks when I wasn't feeling quite so crushed, I definitely still heard that man's voice calling me dangerous and believed my work badge was bugged.
Before this difficult period started two years ago, did you ever hear voices or feel like people were watching, spying on, or bugging you?

No, I never experienced anything like hearing voices or feeling watched before all this started. Before the warehouse restructuring, I was just my usual steady self, focusing on my woodworking, my family, and doing my job. I never had any of those strange experiences back then.

During those few weeks when you felt a bit lighter, did you find that you started to regain any interest in your hobbies, like your woodworking or going to the river, or did you still have no interest in them at all?

No, I still didn't have any interest in them at all. Even though I felt a little lighter, I would go out to the garage, look at my half-built boat, and just feel completely blank. I couldn't bring myself to pick up a tool, so I'd just turn off the light and go back inside.

Aside from that brief period last year, has there ever been any other time over the past two years where you felt completely free of depression, yet you still heard the voice or felt that your badge was bugged?

No, there hasn't been any other time besides that stretch last year. Usually, the heavy depression and the voices go hand-in-hand, and they've just been a constant weight together. That one period was the only exception where my mood lifted a little bit while the other things stayed.
When you believed your work badge was bugged, what did you think was the reason they were tracking or spying on you?
I believed the company was watching me specifically, just waiting for me to make a mistake or screw up. It felt like they were looking for any excuse they could find to get rid of me and push me out.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts were being broadcast out loud so others could hear them, or that someone was putting thoughts directly into your mind?
No, I've never experienced anything like that. I've never felt like my thoughts were being broadcast out loud for others to hear, or that anyone was putting thoughts directly into my head.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a first-episode, chronic (2+ years) severe depressive episode characterized by persistent depressed mood, profound anhedonia, and fatigue, accompanied by psychotic features (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions). A diagnosis of schizoaffective disorder (F25.1) was ruled out because the patient did not experience a period of 2 weeks or more of psychotic symptoms in the absence of significant depressive symptoms (during his slightly 'lighter' period, he still had significant depressive symptoms, including a complete lack of interest/pleasure). Recurrent depressive disorder (F33.3) was ruled out as this is his first lifetime depressive episode.
